description: Commands that stamp nothing still require actor and at: delete, unlink and update without actor report E_MISSING_FIELD, an absent at reports E_MISSING_FIELD, an unparseable at reports E_BAD_TIMESTAMP, and none of them changes the store.
claim moves open to in_progress and stamps assignee from the CLAIMING command's actor — created by art, claimed by jonathan, assignee jonathan, createdBy art.

Re-claiming an in_progress task and reopening it are E_BAD_TRANSITION; an unknown literal id with a bad timestamp co-fires E_BAD_TIMESTAMP and E_UNKNOWN_ID without E_BAD_TRANSITION; an unresolved $-token is an unknown referent; failed commands change nothing.

close stamps closedAt and an optional closeReason; claim stamps survive a close; a non-string reason on a LEGAL target is E_BAD_FIELD alone and closes nothing; a never-claimed task closes straight from open without a closeReason key.
close without a reason leaves no closeReason: an imported open record carrying a stray closeReason "cancelled" and closed plainly reports as done, not cancelled.
Closing or claiming a closed task is E_BAD_TRANSITION; on a known target it CO-FIRES with a non-string reason and an offsetless at in one sorted set; the original close stamps hold throughout.
A comment naming an unknown id is E_UNKNOWN_ID; a comment missing text is E_MISSING_FIELD; an unparseable at is E_BAD_TIMESTAMP; none records anything.
Comments render in submission order even when a later comment carries an earlier at — clock skew never rewrites history.
8 writer processes at once, 100 writes each (comment on 4 shared tasks, update of its own task, close of its own tasks, in turn): every write acknowledged ok is in the store afterwards.
create naming an unknown parent reports E_UNKNOWN_ID — co-fired with field errors when both hold — and creates nothing.

A minimal create takes type task, priority 2, status open, stamps from the command, and no absent-field keys; an explicit create holds exactly what it was given — createdBy is the COMMAND's actor, not a session default.

Absent and mistyped actor, present-but-mistyped required fields, and a lone criterionId are E_MISSING_FIELD; mistyped optionals are E_BAD_FIELD with no existence lookup on the numeric parent; -1 and "high" are E_BAD_PRIORITY; the boundary priority 4 is accepted.

create with parent creates the task and the parent-child edge atomically — and the edge is the SAME edge link sees: re-parenting is E_HAS_PARENT, the identical re-link is a no-op, a cycle through it is E_CYCLE.
delete removes a task entirely: after it, show reports E_UNKNOWN_ID and list is empty — the only way to take an erroneously-created task out of the store.
delete admits a task in any status: an in_progress task and a closed task are both removed with ok true, never E_BAD_TRANSITION.
deleting a blocker cascades its link: the formerly-blocked task becomes ready and shows an empty dependsOn — the graph stays consistent.

delete drops edges at BOTH endpoints and of BOTH types: deleting a parent frees its child (show renders no parent, and the child accepts a new parent), and deleting a task that holds a blocks edge as its dependent removes that edge from export. Deleting that child in turn drops its own parent-child edge, so export ends with no links.
delete on an unknown id reports E_UNKNOWN_ID; a delete missing its id reports E_MISSING_FIELD; neither changes the store.
A create violating four independent rules at once — missing title, mistyped description, unknown type, out-of-range priority — reports all four codes sorted, and the store is unchanged.
Export carries every held field of every task verbatim — linkage, legacyRef, claim stamps, comments — in creation order (the second-created task carries the EARLIER createdAt), with edges in links.
A generated id is never handed out again after delete: create, delete it, create again — the deleted token stays an unknown referent and the new task is a distinct id.

Import holds export-shaped records verbatim under their literal ids in PAYLOAD order (reverse-id here, so an id-sorted import diverges) — and imported tasks are FULL store members: they surface in ready, gate ready through imported blocks edges, project through report, multi-comment submission order survives, and a create against an imported linkage key is a HIT returning the literal imported id.

An import collides only with HELD ids: an id freed by delete may return by import. Keys outside the record's contract fields are dropped on task records and on comments alike, so export renders neither.
An import colliding with a held linkage key and repeating an id within its own payload reports both codes sorted, imports nothing, and leaves the store as it was.

One import payload violating many rules at once reports all ten codes in one sorted set and imports nothing; an envelope missing actor and at is E_MISSING_FIELD; an unparseable envelope at is E_BAD_TIMESTAMP; a record whose ONLY defects are offsetless startedAt/closedAt is E_BAD_TIMESTAMP (stamp parseability is not createdAt-only); a valid empty import succeeds with imported 0; a tasks-absent import is E_MISSING_FIELD; a bad envelope and a bad record CO-FIRE in one sorted set — neither side short-circuits the other.

description: Import links validate against the HELD graph and held ids: a payload link naming a held task resolves; one that would give a held child a second parent is E_HAS_PARENT; one closing a cycle with a held edge is E_CYCLE; one duplicating a held edge is an accepted no-op. Entries apply in payload order: an earlier clean payload edge counts against later entries (a second payload parent is E_HAS_PARENT), and a failed entry never joins (its would-be edge closes no cycle for the entry after it). An entry repeating an EARLIER PAYLOAD edge is an accepted no-op too: a repeated parent-child entry is not E_HAS_PARENT and a repeated blocks entry is stored once.

A linkage-key collision is a lookup and needs both key fields well-typed: an import record whose criterionId is a number, against a held (specItemRef, absent) key, reports E_BAD_FIELD alone — never E_DUP_LINKAGE.

Each import rule witnessed alone — a payload whose ONLY defect is a parent key, a dependsOn key, a comment missing text, a comment with an unparseable at, a mistyped createdBy, a mistyped description, a lone criterionId, a status outside the vocabulary, an unparseable createdAt, a mistyped assignee, a mistyped closeReason, a non-object task record, a non-object comment, or a non-object links entry, a record missing only type, priority, status, id, or createdAt, a comment missing only actor or only at, an envelope missing only at, or a non-string type (E_BAD_TYPE, not E_BAD_FIELD) reports exactly that rule's code; a non-array tasks co-fires with a non-array links; the store stays empty.
Two blocks edges added in an order that disagrees with id order render in EDGE-CREATION order in show.dependsOn and export.links — an id-sorted rendering diverges.
Cycles are refused per type-graph: a blocks chain refuses its closing edge and the self-link; the parent graph accepts the reverse of a blocks edge but refuses its own 2-cycle.

Re-linking an identical edge — blocks or parent-child — is an accepted no-op: one edge each in export, the repeated parent edge is never E_HAS_PARENT, and the no-op diversion happens ONLY for clean commands — an identical edge with a bad at is the error envelope.

Unknown referents report E_UNKNOWN_ID once however many are unknown, co-fired with E_BAD_TYPE for an unknown type; a self-link with an offsetless at co-fires E_BAD_TIMESTAMP and E_CYCLE; an absent type is E_MISSING_FIELD while a numeric type is E_BAD_TYPE; non-string referents are E_MISSING_FIELD with no lookup or graph checks; no edge is recorded.
A second parent-child edge to a DIFFERENT parent is E_HAS_PARENT; a link that would both re-parent and close a parent-graph cycle CO-FIRES E_CYCLE + E_HAS_PARENT; the original parent holds.

Distinct criterionIds and the criterion-less form under one specItemRef are three distinct tasks; replaying the criterion-less key is an idempotent HIT (absent criterionId is a key value); creates with no specItemRef never collide.

Re-creating a held (specItemRef, criterionId) key returns the existing id with created false — before and after the holder closes — the holder's fields survive, a field-INVALID replay of the held key is the error envelope (never a hit), report lists one entry, and the create after the hits takes token $2.

Linkage keys compare as exact pairs: an empty-string criterionId is a present value distinct from an absent one, and a space in either field cannot make two different pairs one key — all four creates are fresh tasks. The empty-string task is created BEFORE the absent one, and report still sorts the absent criterionId first, so creation order cannot stand in for the rule.

Validation precedes idempotency: an idempotent hit carrying a known parent creates NO edge and discards the proposal whole — on an in_progress holder — while the same key with an unknown parent fails E_UNKNOWN_ID outright.

Unfiltered list shows every task in creation order — the timestamps run in reverse, so a createdAt-sorted list diverges — whatever the status; the open filter restricts; a filter outside the vocabulary is E_BAD_FIELD.
create with ask stamps askedBy from the command's actor; ifYes, ifNo and answers are held beside it; an update that sets a new ask restamps askedBy from its actor; show returns every field.

description: ifYes, ifNo or answers with no ask is E_MISSING_FIELD on create and on an update of a task holding none; answers outside yes-no and words is E_BAD_FIELD; a plain field that isn't a string is E_BAD_FIELD; none of them changes the store.
update with an empty string clears a plain field; clearing the ask clears ifYes, ifNo, answers and askedBy with it; replacing goal leaves why alone.
import holds the plain fields and askedBy verbatim and export returns them; a mistyped plain field or an answers outside its two words is E_BAD_FIELD and imports nothing.
create holds goal, why and doneWhen verbatim; show returns them, list, search and ready carry goal; a task without them omits the keys; an empty string on create is as if absent.

description: A fractional priority (2.5) is E_BAD_PRIORITY on create and on update — a priority is an integer 0..4 by value, not merely a number in range.

An open blocker excludes the dependent; a merely claimed blocker still excludes it; with TWO blockers the dependent stays excluded until BOTH close — blockers are a conjunction, never released on the first unblock.
Epics never appear in ready — even at priority 0, where wrong inclusion would head the queue; their children do. The exclusion is ready-only: an epic claims and closes like any task.
ready ties break by creation order, never id order: imported literal ids legacy-b then legacy-a, equal priority, surface b before a.
parent-child edges never gate readiness: a non-epic parent and its child are both ready.
ready sorts by priority ascending, ties by creation order ascending — the equal-priority pair carries timestamps in REVERSE creation order, so a createdAt-sorted queue diverges.
in_progress and closed tasks never appear in ready.

Closing the DIRECT blocker releases the dependent — blocking is one edge deep, never the transitive closure: the head of a chain is ready when its own blocker closes, whatever the far upstream's status.

reopen returns a claimed-then-closed task to open with every claim and close stamp removed — and ONLY those: description, legacyRef, priority, and comments survive; reopening an open task is E_BAD_TRANSITION.
report lists only spec-linked tasks, sorted by (specItemRef, criterionId, taskRef) with the keyless entry first, statuses projected.
Only closeReason exactly "cancelled" projects to cancelled — "shipped" and "Cancelled" project to done; the match is full-string and case-sensitive.

report compares keys in Unicode code-point order: 'spec:B' before 'spec:a' (no case folding, no locale collation), and U+FFFD before U+1F600 (an astral character sorts after every BMP character, which UTF-16 code-unit comparison reverses).

Importing an export-shaped payload into an empty store and exporting yields the payload exactly, in payload order (reverse-id) — claim stamps included, and a stamp-inconsistent record (open with a stray closeReason) held verbatim: cross-consistency is the exporter's business, never re-validated or repaired.
search matches q as a case-insensitive substring over the text-bearing fields (id/title/description/specItemRef/criterionId/legacyRef); a no-match returns [] and a missing q reports E_MISSING_FIELD.
search reads ONLY id, title, description, specItemRef, criterionId and legacyRef: a term present only in a comment, a closeReason, an assignee, createdBy, the type, or the status finds nothing.

search folds case on BOTH sides (an uppercase stored title matches a lowercase query), reaches description, specItemRef, legacyRef and id, restricts by status, and co-fires E_BAD_FIELD with E_MISSING_FIELD when q is missing and status is invalid.
show renders exactly the held keys — every optional present when held, absent otherwise — and an unknown id is E_UNKNOWN_ID with task null.

create holds source verbatim and show and export return it; an empty source on create is as if absent; update sets a source on a task without one, replaces one, and clears it with an empty string; list entries never carry it.
import holds a record's source verbatim and export returns it; an empty, malformed or non-string source is E_BAD_FIELD alone and imports nothing.

a source that isn't a string, has no colon, an empty or 33-character kind, a kind starting with a digit or -, a capital, an empty or 201-character value, or a space or U+00A0 in the value is E_BAD_FIELD on create and update, changing nothing; a 32-character kind with digits and - and a 200-character value is held.

An offsetless date-time and a leap-second date-time are both unparseable per the felag-core Timestamps rule: E_BAD_TIMESTAMP, nothing created — and the success that follows two failures normalizes to $1, not $3.

Parseable is RFC 3339's grammar, field ranges included: hour 24, 30 February, 29 February outside a leap year (2025, and 2100 — divisible by 100, not by 400), month 13, an offset of +24:00, and offset minutes of 60 are each E_BAD_TIMESTAMP; 29 February in 2024 and in 2000 (divisible by 400), and 23:59:59 with a -23:59 offset, are accepted verbatim.

Non-Z offsets and lowercase t/z designators are stored and returned verbatim on EVERY at-valued field — createdAt, startedAt, closedAt, comment ats, and imported stamps alike — never normalized to UTC, never upcased, through show and export both.
unclaim moves in_progress back to open and clears assignee and startedAt.

unclaim on an open task and on a closed task both return E_BAD_TRANSITION, and its error plumbing matches its sibling verbs: E_UNKNOWN_ID alone for an unknown id, co-firing with a bad clock, and the transition check NOT evaluated when the referent is unknown. Failed commands change nothing.
A command whose op is absent or names no command in the contract reports E_BAD_FIELD in the bare {ok, errors} envelope and changes nothing.

unlink removes the edge link records: the blocks removal un-gates the dependent in ready, the parent-child removal orphans the child and leaves it re-parentable, and a repeat is accepted with removed false.
unlink is NOT total across delete: replaying an unlink whose dependsOn was deleted reports E_UNKNOWN_ID, not a quiet success — the held-referent rule outranks the link/unlink symmetry.

unlink validates as link does — unknown referents (once, however many), missing and unknown type, the co-firing pair, a non-string referent with no lookup, and a bad timestamp — every one with removed false, and the held edge survives all of them.

unlink matches the (id, dependsOn, type) triple EXACTLY while the edge is still held: reversed referents and the wrong type each report removed false and the edge survives export; only the exact triple removes it.
update replaces exactly the named fields on a task of any status — open, in_progress, and closed — overrides a claim-set assignee, and never touches status or stamps.
An empty, absent, or non-object set is E_MISSING_FIELD; a set naming status is E_BAD_FIELD; an out-of-range priority and a non-string title co-fire sorted; the task is unchanged.
